title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rope-fused-ops-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: - Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops and improved memory layout. - Add KV-batching-aware scheduler and continuous-batching fallbacks to reduce p99 latency tail. - New runtime flags to toggle kernel variants and conservative rollout plan (canary -> gradual).
description: Motivation: shipping lower-latency, higher-throughput inference across our hosted and dedicated deployments requires updating the attention implementation to the latest FlashAttentionV2 variants and taking advantage of fused rotary/rope ops. This PR upgrades the attention kernels, adds fused op paths for rotary/rope embeddings, and integrates a KV-batching-aware scheduling policy and continuous-batching fallbacks. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce FlashAttentionV2 kernels under runtime/attn/flashattn_v2 with CPU/GPU build targets and CUDA kernels compiled with sm80+ optimizations. 2) Add fused rotary and rope code paths to reduce elementwise kernels and copying for common transformer variants. 3) Implement KV-batching scheduler heuristics in serving/scheduler that group small KV cache hits into batched GPU kernels while preserving low-latency fast-paths for short-context requests. 4) Add a continuous-batching fallback that trades off throughput/latency at high QPS to keep GPUs saturated while respecting per-request latency SLOs. 5) Runtime flags and feature gate: runtime.attn.kernel=(legacy|flashattnv2), runtime.attn.fused_rotary=(true|false), runtime.scheduler.kv_batching=(auto|off|on). 6) Extensive perf harness and benchmark scripts (perf/benchmarks/attn) and new microbenchmarks for KV hit/miss behavior. Compatibility and safety: default is conservative (legacy kernel) and rollout is gated by an operator feature flag. The PR includes a canary pipeline that runs the perf lab against a representative trace before enabling platform-wide. Perf results (representative): - GPT-NeoX-like, seq=2048, A100: throughput +14% tokens/sec; p99 latency -18% (from 340ms to 280ms) at 8 concurrent streams. - LLaMA-style, seq=4096, A100: memory usage reduced by ~9% enabling larger effective context per-GPU. - KV-heavy workloads (short prompts with long histories): end-to-end tail latency reduction ~12% due to KV batching and fused ops. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated pool (10% traffic) for 48 hours -> expand to 30% with monitoring -> full rollout. If any metric regresses beyond thresholds (p99 latency +5% or error rate +0.5%), the feature gate will be revoked automatically. Related work: ENG-4791 (kernel upgrade), ENG-4810 (scheduler/kvcache improvements).

testing_summary: Unit tests added for new shader paths and fused ops. Integration tests exercise KV batching heuristics with synthetic traces including high KV-hit and high KV-miss ratios. Benchmarks run on perf lab A100 pool across multiple seeds; numbers are averages across 5 runs. Canary run executed on 2026-02-18 against production-like trace: no regressions; kv_batch.hit_rate reported stable; p99 improvements observed. Driver-version safeguard tested by simulating older CUDA drivers in CI docker images.
change_summary: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2, add fused rotary/rope ops, implement KV-batching-aware scheduler and continuous batching fallback, expose runtime flags and feature gate, add perf harness and canary pipeline.
motivation: Improve inference throughput and reduce p99 latency tails for diverse workloads (short prompts with long histories and long-context batches) without increasing operational complexity.
notes_for_ops: Default behavior unchanged until feature gate enabled. Operators can toggle runtime.attn.kernel and runtime.scheduler.kv_batching via feature flags; canary pipeline is provided. Watch p99 latency, error rate, and kv_batch.hit_rate when enabling. Driver guard will prevent enabling FlashAttentionV2 on unsupported hosts.
examples_and_bench_instructions: See perf/benchmarks/attn/README.md (added) and run: ./perf/benchmarks/attn/run_bench.sh --model gpt-neox --seq 2048 --runs 5 --kernel flashattnv2
